directAnswer: Pope Donus was a Roman who reigned from 676 to 678. The Liber Pontificalis records his restoration of Roman churches, including paving the atrium of St. Peter's with marble, and the return of the archbishop of Ravenna to obedience to Rome.

sections.h2: Marble for the Atrium of St. Peter's
paras: Donus was the son of a Roman named Mauricius and was elderly when he was consecrated in November 676, after a vacancy of more than four months. The Liber Pontificalis credits him with paving the great atrium in front of St. Peter's, known as the paradise, with marble, and with restoring other churches, including the church of the Apostles on the Via Ostiensis and Sant'Eufemia on the Via Appia.

sections.h2: Ravenna's Return and Nestorian Monks in Rome
paras: During his reign, the same source says, Archbishop Reparatus of Ravenna returned to obedience to the Roman see, beginning the end of the independence Ravenna had claimed under Pope Vitalian. Donus also discovered that a monastery in Rome known as the Boetiana housed Syrian monks holding Nestorian views; he dispersed them among other monasteries and gave the house to Roman monks.

Emperor Constantine IV wrote to Donus proposing a conference to settle the dispute over Christ's wills, a step that would lead to the Third Council of Constantinople, but the letter arrived only after Donus had died on 11 April 678. He was buried in St. Peter's. Little else is known of him.

keyFacts: Born in Rome, son of Mauricius
Paved the atrium of Old St. Peter's with marble
Archbishop Reparatus of Ravenna returned to obedience to Rome
Constantine IV's letter proposing a council arrived after his death

faqs.question: What did Pope Donus do for St. Peter's Basilica?
faqs.answer: According to the Liber Pontificalis, he paved the large courtyard in front of Old St. Peter's, called the paradise, with marble.

faqs.question: How did Donus' reign affect Ravenna?
faqs.answer: Archbishop Reparatus of Ravenna, whose see had been granted independence from Rome under Constans II, returned to obedience to the pope during Donus' pontificate.
